newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 7.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
- No matter how the dumping lawsuit brought by Cray Research Inc against a Japanese supercomputer maker is resolved, it appears Cray may end up the loser.
- The Raytheon Co has won the bidding for Texas Instruments military business, but victory may have come at a rich price.
- H. Wayne Huizenga's Republic Industries announced an agreement to buy National Car Rental System for $600 million in stock.
- From General Electric to Wang, companies that a few years ago got almost all their profits from selling widgets are rapidly transforming themselves into service providers.
- The auto industry ended the year with a 4 percent drop in sales.
- Shares of Toys R Us tumbled 14.6 percent in active trading after the big toy retailer said its Christmas sales were flat.
- Monsanto agreed to buy Holden's Foundation Seeds, a major producer of corn seed, and two Holden seed distributors, for $1.02 billion.
- Apple Computer shares fell more than 20 percent following the company's disclosure that it would report a loss in what is typically its strongest quarter.
- Texaco named the BBDO Worldwide unit of Omnicom Group as its lead corporate agency.
- A Federal judge fined the Prudential Insurance Co $1 million after several incidents of document destruction in the company's long-running legal dispute over deceptive sales practices.

- Four years ago, many top economists criticized President Clinton's selection of Laura D'Andrea Tyson as chairman of his Council of Economic Advisors, but when he chose Janet Yellen to replace Ms. Tyson, the move made barely a ripple among economists.
- Prosecutors in Germany announced fraud charges against Jurgen Schneider, the real estate developer whose empire collapsed nearly three years ago in one of Germany's biggest corporate scandals.
